extracted.intended_audience: researchers and practitioners in information retrieval / NLP and news publishers interested in headline quality and engagement
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluating and predicting the quality of news article headlines using behavioral engagement signals (click count, dwell time) derived from website logs and modeling semantic relation between headline and article body.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engagement-based headline quality indicators
rubrics_metrics.description: Four indicators to determine the quality of published news headlines based on their click count and dwell time, which are obtained by website log analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paper proposes deriving quality indicators from website logs (clicks and dwell time). These indicators are used as targets (soft target distribution) to train a model that predicts headline quality. Exact formulations of the four indicators are not listed on this page excerpt.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoiding misleading headlines (no clickbait)
rubrics_metrics.description: Headlines should not be misleading (e.g., clickbaits); otherwise, readers would be disappointed when reading the content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quality assessment must consider whether the headline accurately reflects article content; high click counts alone are insufficient if they result from misleading phrasing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Semantic relation between headline and body
rubrics_metrics.description: The model considers the semantic relation between headline and body as part of predicting headline quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessments should measure how well the headline semantically aligns with the article body; semantic consistency is a feature predictive of quality and non-misleadingness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of latent features from headline and body
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed model processes the latent features of both headline and body of the article to predict its headline quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Feature engineering / representation learning should capture latent aspects of both headline text and body text (not just surface statistics) to improve prediction of headline quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Soft target distribution training objective
rubrics_metrics.description: Use soft target distribution of the calculated quality indicators to train the deep learning model which can predict the quality of unpublished news headlines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instead of hard labels, train models on a distributional/soft target derived from engagement-based indicators (clicks, dwell time) to better represent nuanced quality signals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Empirical evaluation on real-world newsroom logs
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate models using a real dataset from a major newspaper (website logs) to validate that the proposed method outperforms other state-of-the-art NLP models.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quality measures and model performance should be validated on authentic publisher data (clicks, dwell times) rather than synthetic or small-scale datasets.
